decisions.choice: four days in the tomb: Lazarus was beyond any doubt dead
alternatives: four days: a detail with no further point
decisions.reason: In Judea the dead were buried on the day they died, because of the heat (compare Acts 5:6-10). So Lazarus had been dead four days, and the body had begun to decay, as Martha says in 11:39. No one could think he was only unconscious. The count also shows that Jesus came too late for any ordinary help (11:21).

decisions.choice: a belief that the soul stayed near the body for three days may lie behind the count
decisions.reason: Later rabbinic writings (Genesis Rabbah 100:7; Leviticus Rabbah 18:1) record a belief that the soul hovers near the body for three days, hoping to return, and leaves when the face changes. If the belief was held in Jesus's day, the fourth day would mean that all hope was gone. These writings come from centuries later, so it is not certain that the belief was current then; the point of 11:39 stands without it.

decisions.choice: him ... having four days: he had already been there four days
decisions.reason: The verb "to have" with a length of time is the ordinary Greek way of saying how long something has lasted, as in 5:5-6. "Him" is Lazarus, named in 11:1-14. The reckoning fits the story: the messenger's journey, the two days Jesus stayed where he was (11:6), and his own journey to Bethany.

decisions.choice: [Lazarus] (L); Lazarus (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "him"; after "Jesus" an English pronoun would be unclear, so every level names Lazarus, Literal in brackets.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "you" when people speak to him; this applies throughout the passage. Literal keeps the Greek participle and needs no pronoun.

decisions.choice: [Lázaro] (L); Lázaro (B, R); llevaba cuatro días
decisions.reason: As in English: names Lazarus. "Llevar" + time is the Greek idiom of "having" four days (meaning decision m3), as at 5:5.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("Jésus lui dit", "Marthe lui dit", 11:23-27); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (11:17-27), as in 1:19. The passé simple ("trouva", "alla", "répondit") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal keeps the present where John tells a past event in the present (verses 23, 24, 27), as the English Literal does. Readable uses the passé composé ("Jésus est arrivé"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. The pluperfect ("étaient venus", verse 19) and the imperfect ("était assise", verse 20) are used at every level for what lay behind or around the scene.

decisions.choice: le tombeau (L, B); la tombe (R)
decisions.reason: The tomb was a cave closed with a stone (11:38), for which French "tombeau" is the usual word; "sépulcre" is literary. Readable says "la tombe", the everyday word.

decisions.choice: "mộ" for mnēmeion
decisions.reason: "mộ" is the plain word for a grave or tomb; the meaning of a cave tomb comes out in 11:38.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; "께서" and the honorific -시- carry respect for Jesus
alternatives: deity_pronoun spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7); recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: "he" is in the verb ("አገኘ")
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader's setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change in Amharic. Pronouns for God and for Jesus are written plainly throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span; honorific "उन्होंने", "आप" for Jesus
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus is shown by the honorific third person and by "आप" at every level, as the style guide sets out; God, spoken of in 11:22, is honorific too. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "[Лазарь]"
decisions.reason: The Greek says "him"; after "Иисус" a Russian pronoun would be unclear, so every level names Lazarus, Literal in brackets.

decisions.choice: "来られて", "見いだされた" (L); "来てみられる" (B); "着かれる" (R)
decisions.reason: As throughout John in Japanese, the narrator uses light respect forms (〜れる / 〜られる, お〜になる) for what Jesus and God do, at every level, and for no one else. This holds through the passage.

decisions.choice: "[ラザロが]" (L); "ラザロ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "him"; Japanese avoids 彼 and names Lazarus, Literal in brackets.

decisions.choice: fifteen stadia: a little less than two miles
decisions.reason: A stadion was about 600 feet (185 meters), so fifteen of them come to about 1.7 miles (2.8 kilometers). Bethany lay on the eastern slope of the Mount of Olives, on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho.

decisions.choice: this Bethany: the village of Martha and Mary near Jerusalem
decisions.reason: John has already named another Bethany, beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing (1:28) and where Jesus has been staying (10:40). By saying how close this one is to Jerusalem, John makes clear which place he means, and why it was dangerous for Jesus to go there (11:7-8, 16). It also explains why so many came from the city to mourn (verse 19).

decisions.choice: was: the past tense of the story
alternatives: Bethany no longer stood when John wrote
decisions.reason: John tells the whole story in the past, so the past tense is natural here. It need not mean that the village no longer existed when he wrote; contrast 5:2, where he describes a place with "is".

decisions.choice: about fifteen stadia off: at a distance of about fifteen stadia
decisions.reason: The word "from" placed before the measure is a Greek way of giving the distance between two places (compare 21:8), not the starting point of a journey.

decisions.choice: about {{units:2 miles|fifteen stadia}}
decisions.reason: As at 6:19: Balanced and Readable give the distance in miles by default, rounded as the Greek "about" allows, and the units setting shows the original measure. Numerals are used in measurements. Literal always keeps the ancient unit.

decisions.choice: unos {{units:3 kilómetros|quince estadios}}
decisions.reason: As at 6:19: fifteen stadia are about 2.8 kilometers (meaning decision m1), given in kilometers by default.

decisions.choice: à environ {{units:3 kilomètres|quinze stades}}
decisions.reason: French readers measure distance in kilometres, so the modern default is metric, not the miles of the English. A stade was about 185 metres, so fifteen of them come to about 2.8 kilometres (meaning decision m1), rounded to "3 kilomètres" as the Greek "about" allows. The units setting shows the original measure; Literal always keeps the ancient unit.

decisions.choice: {{units:kilomita tatu|stadia kumi na tano}}
decisions.reason: Fifteen stadia is a little under three kilometres. As in 6:19, the metric figure is the default and the original measure the alternative; Literal keeps the stadia.

decisions.choice: "{{units:3 km|mười lăm ếch-ta-đơ}}": metric by default, the original unit as the alternative; Literal keeps "mười lăm ếch-ta-đơ"
decisions.reason: Style guide section 7: Vietnamese readers measure in kilometres, so the default differs from the English (US miles). Fifteen stadia is about 2.8 km, rounded to 3 km as the Greek "about" allows; "ếch-ta-đơ" transliterates stadion.

decisions.choice: {{units:3킬로미터|십오 스타디온}} (metric by default, the original unit as the alternative)
decisions.reason: The style guide sets metric as the Korean default, as in French and Swahili, unlike the English (US units). Fifteen stadia is about 2.8 km, rounded to 3. Literal keeps the original unit.

decisions.choice: {{units:3 quilômetros|quinze estádios}}
decisions.reason: The Portuguese default is metric (style section 7), unlike the English miles: fifteen stadia are about 2.8 kilometres (meaning decision m1), rounded to 3 as the Greek "about" allows. The units setting gives the original measure; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: "አሥራ አምስት ምዕራፍ" (fifteen stadia, L); {{units:3 ኪሎ ሜትር|አሥራ አምስት ምዕራፍ}} (B, R)
alternatives: "2 ማይል" (2 miles), as the English default
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for Amharic: metric by default, the original unit as the alternative, where the English has US units. Fifteen stadia are a little under 3 kilometres. "ምዕራፍ" is the established Amharic word for the Greek stadion; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: {{units:3 किलोमीटर|पंद्रह स्टेडियम}} (B, R); "पंद्रह स्टेडियम" (L)
decisions.reason: Hindi gives distances in metric units by default, with the original measure as the alternative, as the style guide sets out; fifteen stadia is a little under 3 kilometres, rounded as the Greek "about" allows. Literal keeps the original unit. This differs from the English, which uses miles.

decisions.choice: "трёх километрах", with "пятнадцати стадиях" as the units alternative
decisions.reason: The English gives miles by default; Russian, as the style guide sets out (section 7), gives the metric distance by default, rounded as the Greek "about" allows (fifteen stadia is a little under three kilometres), with the original measure as the alternative. Literal keeps the stadia.

decisions.choice: приблизно за {{units:три кілометри|пʼятнадцять стадій}}, metric by default
decisions.reason: The Ukrainian units setting is metric by default, unlike the English (US miles); fifteen stadia is a little under 3 km. Literal keeps the Greek unit.

decisions.choice: {{units:3キロメートル|十五スタディオン}}ほど (B, R)
alternatives: {{units:約3キロメートル|十五スタディオン}}
decisions.reason: Japanese readers measure in metric, so the units setting gives kilometers by default, unlike the English (miles); the original measure is the alternative. "ほど" stays outside the span so that both options keep the Greek "about". Literal keeps the ancient unit. Arabic digits are used only in the modern measure.

decisions.choice: {{units:tiga kilometer|lima belas stadia}} (B, R); "lima belas stadia" with no span (L)
decisions.reason: m1: fifteen stadia is about 2.8 kilometers. As at 6:19, the default is metric, rounded, with the Greek unit as the alternative, against the English miles.

vi.L: Và nhiều người trong số người Do Thái đã đến với Ma-thê và Ma-ri để an ủi họ về [người] anh [của họ].

ko.L: 그리고 유대인들 가운데 많은 사람이 형제의 일로 그들을 위로하려고 마르다와 마리아에게 와 있었다.

pt.L: E muitos dos judeus tinham vindo até Marta e Maria, para consolá-las a respeito do irmão.

ru.L: Многие же из иудеев пришли к Марфе и Марии, чтобы утешить их о брате [их].

uk.L: А багато з юдеїв прийшли до Марти й Марії, щоб утішити їх щодо [їхнього] брата.
uk.B: Багато юдеїв прийшли до Марти й Марії, щоб розрадити їх у горі за братом.

ja.L: そして、ユダヤ人たちのうちの多くの者が、[彼女たちの]兄弟のことで二人を慰めるために、マルタとマリアのところに来ていた。

id.L: Banyak orang Yahudi telah datang kepada Marta dan Maria untuk menghibur mereka karena saudara mereka.
id.B: Banyak orang Yahudi telah datang kepada Marta dan Maria untuk menghibur mereka atas kematian saudara mereka.
id.R: Banyak orang Yahudi datang dari Yerusalem untuk menghibur Marta dan Maria, karena saudara mereka meninggal.

decisions.choice: the Jews: Jewish people from Jerusalem and the country around, who had come to mourn
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: Here the word means neither the people as a whole nor the authorities, but the friends and neighbors who came to comfort the sisters; verse 18 points to Jerusalem as the place most had come from. They are the same group who follow Mary to the tomb and weep with her (11:31, 33). Afterwards many of them believe in Jesus, while some report to the Pharisees (11:45-46). Martha, Mary and Lazarus are Jews too.

decisions.choice: to console them: the duty of comforting mourners
decisions.reason: Mourning for the dead lasted seven days (Genesis 50:10; 1 Samuel 31:13; Sirach 22:12), and friends and neighbors came to sit with the family and comfort them (Job 2:11-13). That so many had come suggests the family was well known and loved.

decisions.choice: had come: they were already there when Jesus arrived
decisions.reason: The pluperfect looks back from the moment of Jesus's arrival: the mourners were already in the house. This sets up the story that follows, in which they see what Jesus does (11:31, 36-37, 45).

decisions.choice: to Martha and Mary (SBLGNT)
alternatives: to those around Martha and Mary
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "to those around Martha and Mary", a Greek way of naming the sisters together with their household. The sense is the same, so no footnote. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Many Jews (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the mourners present in the house (meaning decision m1), not the authorities and not the Jewish people as a whole. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and tie it to the people present, as 8:48 and 10:31 do, so no footnote is needed.

decisions.choice: from Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable says where the mourners had come from, which verse 18 implies. Some of them may have lived in Bethany itself, so this goes a little beyond what the verse states.

decisions.choice: los judíos / muchos judíos
decisions.reason: Here the word means the mourners (meaning decision m1), not the authorities, so no "dirigentes".

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); beaucoup de Juifs (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the friends and neighbours who came to mourn with the sisters (meaning decision m1), not the authorities, so no level speaks of leaders. Balanced and Readable say "beaucoup de Juifs", as the English does: the sisters and their brother are Jews too, and the word names the mourners present.

decisions.choice: "người Do Thái" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision finds Jewish people who came to mourn, not the authorities, so B and R keep the people's name.

decisions.choice: "많은 유대인" (B, R), not "유대 지도자들"
decisions.reason: Here the word means Jewish people who came to mourn (meaning decision), so every level says "유대인".

decisions.choice: "አይሁድ" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "the Jews" here as Jewish people who came to mourn, not the authorities, so every level keeps the word. Used for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "यहूदी" at every level
decisions.reason: Here the word means the mourners who had come to the house (meaning decision m1), not the authorities, so every level says "यहूदी".

decisions.choice: "иудеи" at every level
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish mourners who had come to the house (meaning decision m1), not the authorities, so every level keeps "иудеи".

decisions.choice: "ユダヤ人たち" (L); "ユダヤ人" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the mourners (m1), not the authorities, so Balanced and Readable say ユダヤ人 rather than ユダヤ人の指導者たち. Literal always keeps ユダヤ人たち.

source.text: ἡ οὖν Μάρθα ὡς ἤκουσεν ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἔρχεται ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ· Μαρία δὲ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ ἐκαθέζετο.

en.R: When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But Mary stayed at home, sitting in the house.

es.B: Cuando Marta oyó que Jesús venía, salió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} encuentro, mientras María se quedó sentada en casa.
es.R: Cuando Marta oyó que Jesús venía, salió a encontrarlo. Pero María se quedó en casa, sentada.

ko.L: 그래서 마르다는 예수께서 오신다는 것을 듣고 그분을 맞이하였고, 마리아는 집 안에 앉아 있었다.

pt.B: Quando Marta soube que Jesus estava chegando, ela saiu ao encontro {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, enquanto Maria ficou sentada em casa.

ru.L: Итак, Марфа, когда услышала, что Иисус идёт, вышла {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}} навстречу; Мария же сидела в доме.

id.L: Ketika Marta mendengar bahwa Yesus datang, ia pergi menyongsong {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}; tetapi Maria tetap duduk di rumah.
id.B: Ketika Marta mendengar bahwa Yesus sedang datang, ia pergi menyongsong {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}, sedangkan Maria tetap duduk di rumah.

decisions.choice: that Jesus is coming: the words as Martha heard them
decisions.reason: Greek keeps the tense of the words that were spoken when it reports them, so "is coming" is what Martha was told. It is not the historic present of storytelling.

decisions.choice: met him: went out to meet him on the road
decisions.reason: The verb means to go to meet someone. Jesus had not yet entered the village (11:30), so Martha left the house and the mourners and went out to him.

decisions.choice: Mary was sitting: the posture of a mourner
alternatives: Mary refused to go out to Jesus
decisions.reason: Mourners sat on the ground or at home while friends came to them (Job 2:8, 13; Ezra 9:3-4; Lamentations 2:10). John does not say why Mary stayed; she may not have heard that Jesus had come, since Martha later tells her quietly (11:28-29). The two sisters act much as they do in Luke 10:38-42, Martha busy and Mary sitting.

decisions.choice: went out to meet
decisions.reason: Brings out the sense of the verb (meaning decision m2): Martha left the village to meet Jesus on the way.

decisions.choice: stayed sitting (B); stayed at home, sitting in the house (R)
decisions.reason: The imperfect describes Mary going on sitting while Martha went out; "stayed" shows the contrast between the sisters.

decisions.choice: le salió al encuentro / salió a encontrarlo
decisions.reason: As in English: Martha left the village to meet him on the road (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the present "viene" as Martha heard it (m1).

decisions.choice: alla à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre
decisions.reason: French says "aller à la rencontre de quelqu’un" with a possessive, so the pronoun for Jesus becomes "sa", agreeing with "rencontre", and takes the deity_pronoun setting where the English has "him". Literal keeps the present "arrive" of the words Martha heard (meaning decision m1).

en.R: Martha said to Jesus, "Lord, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had been here, my brother would still be alive.

fr.R: Marthe a dit à Jésus : « Seigneur, si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} avais été ici, mon frère serait encore vivant.

ko.R: 마르다가 예수께 말했다. "주님, 주님께서 여기 계셨더라면 제 형제는 지금도 살아 있을 것입니다.

pt.B: Marta disse a Jesus: "Senhor, se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} estivesses aqui, o meu irmão não teria morrido.

decisions.choice: and now: even now, after his death
alternatives: and now, as a weak link with no special sense
decisions.reason: "Now" sets the present, with Lazarus four days dead, against what might have been (verse 21). Whatever had happened, Martha's trust in Jesus has not been lost.

decisions.choice: Martha trusts Jesus completely, without saying what she hopes for
alternatives: she expects Jesus to raise Lazarus at once
decisions.reason: She may be hinting that Jesus could ask God to give Lazarus back to life now. But when Jesus speaks of his rising she thinks of the last day (verse 24), and at the tomb she objects that the body has begun to decay (11:39). So her words are more likely a general statement of trust, which leaves room for more than she dares to ask. The text does not settle it, and every level keeps it open.

decisions.choice: ask: the ordinary word for making a request
decisions.reason: Martha uses the usual word for asking something of a superior, the word Jesus uses for the disciples asking the Father (14:13-14; 16:23-24). When John reports Jesus's own prayers, he uses a different verb, the word for asking among equals (14:16; 16:26; 17:9). Martha speaks of Jesus as one whose prayers God hears (compare 9:31); she does not yet see all that he is, though his own prayer at the tomb shows that God does hear him (11:41-42).

decisions.choice: and now (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts begin "But even now", adding the word for "but". The sense hardly changes, so no footnote. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} for God
decisions.reason: "You" is Jesus, and "him" (Balanced) and "he" (Readable) are God, so all take the deity_pronoun setting. Balanced and Readable name God once and then use a pronoun, where the Greek repeats "God"; Literal keeps the repetition.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}
decisions.reason: The stressed "él" is God, so it takes the setting, and so do "le" for God and "te" for Jesus, by the book-wide rule for Spanish (see 8:12); the verbs for Jesus need no subject pronoun in Spanish.

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}" for God in Martha's words; "Chúa" for Jesus without a span
decisions.reason: God takes the reader setting as in the narrative; the title "Chúa" stands for "you" and is always capitalised.

decisions.choice: "神はかなえてくださる" (B); "神はそれをあなたに与えてくださる" (R)
alternatives: "神はあなたにお与えになる" at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek's "God will give to you". Balanced says "grant" as Japanese speaks of a request; Readable keeps "give" with "それを" for the thing asked. Martha's polite speech gives God the respect forms.

only the raising of Lazarus now
decisions.reason: The words could be the usual comfort of a friend who shares the hope of resurrection, and Martha takes them so (verse 24). But Jesus means more: he will raise Lazarus now, as a sign of the life he gives (11:4, 43-44). John lets the words hold both senses, as he often does with Jesus's sayings (2:19-21; 3:3-4).

decisions.choice: rise: stand up again from death
decisions.reason: The verb means to rise or stand up, and is a regular word for rising from the dead (6:39-40; 20:9). The noun "resurrection" in verse 24 comes from the same root.

decisions.choice: told (B); said (R); also answered (verse 24) and said (verse 27)
decisions.reason: John often tells a story in the present tense ("he says") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told in this language. This applies to every such verb in the passage (verses 23, 24 and 27).

decisions.choice: rise again (B); rise from the dead (R)
decisions.reason: "Rise" alone is unclear in English. Balanced uses the phrase "rise again", which names rising from death; Readable says it plainly. Literal keeps the bare verb.

decisions.choice: resucitará
decisions.reason: English needs "rise again" or "rise from the dead"; Spanish "resucitar" already says it (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: ressuscitera (every level)
decisions.reason: English needs "rise again" or "rise from the dead" because "rise" alone is unclear; French "ressusciter" is an everyday word for rising from death and shares its root with "résurrection" in verse 24, as the Greek verb and noun do (meaning decision m2). It also keeps both senses open (m1): the comfort of the last day, and what Jesus is about to do.

decisions.choice: historic present: "nói" with no time word (L, here and in 11:24, 11:27); B and R tell it as past through context
decisions.reason: Vietnamese verbs do not mark tense; Literal does not add "đã", as the style guide asks. One decision for the passage.

decisions.reason: anistemi is to stand up again; Literal keeps the plain verb, and Balanced and Readable say what it means here in everyday words, keeping the noun "부활" for 11:24-25.

decisions.reason: docs/john-terms.md: Literal keeps John's historic present, Balanced and Readable use the past; noted once in this passage.

decisions.choice: "воскресне"
decisions.reason: The verb for rising from death; "воскреснути" is the plain Ukrainian word and ties to "воскресіння" in 11:24-25. Readable adds "з мертвих", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "言われる" (L); "言われた" (B); "言われました" (R)
decisions.reason: John tells the story in the present tense for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable tell it in the past, as Japanese narrative does. This applies to every such verb in the passage (verses 23, 24 and 27).

decisions.choice: "よみがえる" (L, B); "死から生き返る" (R)
decisions.reason: "Rise" here is rising from death (m2), which よみがえる says without a bare "stand up". Readable says it in everyday words. The noun in verse 24 is 復活.

records.literal_gloss: Says to him the Martha, "I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day."

en.L: Martha says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day."

en.R: Martha answered, "I know that he will come back to life on the last day, when the dead rise."

fr.R: Marthe a répondu : « Je sais qu’il reviendra à la vie au dernier jour, quand les morts ressusciteront. »

sw.L: Martha anamwambia, "Najua kwamba atafufuka katika ufufuo wa siku ya mwisho."

ko.L: 마르다가 그분께 말한다. "마지막 날 부활 때에 그가 일어날 줄을 저는 압니다."

pt.R: Marta respondeu: "Eu sei que ele vai voltar a viver no último dia, quando os mortos se levantarem."

hi.L: मार्था उनसे कहती है, "मैं जानती हूँ कि अंतिम दिन पुनरुत्थान में वह जी उठेगा।"
hi.B: मार्था ने उत्तर दिया, "मैं जानती हूँ कि जब मरे हुए जिलाए जाएँगे, तब अंतिम दिन वह जी उठेगा।"
hi.R: मार्था ने जवाब दिया, "मैं जानती हूँ कि अंतिम दिन, जब मरे हुए जी उठेंगे, तब वह भी फिर से ज़िंदा हो जाएगा।"

ru.L: Говорит {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}} Марфа: «Знаю, что воскреснет в воскресение, в последний день.»
ru.B: Марфа ответила: «Я знаю, что он воскреснет, когда воскреснут мёртвые, в последний день.»
ru.R: Марфа ответила: «Я знаю, что он оживёт в последний день, когда воскреснут все мёртвые.»

uk.L: Каже {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}} Марта: «Знаю, що він воскресне у воскресінні в останній день.»
uk.B: Марта відповіла: «Я знаю, що він воскресне, коли воскреснуть мертві, в останній день.»
uk.R: Марта відповіла: «Я знаю, що він оживе в останній день, коли мертві воскреснуть.»

ja.L: マルタは[イエス]に言う。「終わりの日の復活のときに、[兄弟が]よみがえることは知っています。」
ja.B: マルタは答えた。「死んだ人々がよみがえる終わりの日に、兄弟もよみがえることは知っています。」
ja.R: マルタは答えました。「終わりの日に死んだ人たちが生き返るとき、兄弟も生き返ることは知っています。」

id.L: Marta berkata kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, "Aku tahu bahwa ia akan bangkit pada waktu kebangkitan pada hari terakhir."
id.B: Marta menjawab, "Aku tahu ia akan bangkit ketika orang-orang mati dibangkitkan, pada hari terakhir."
id.R: Marta menjawab, "Aku tahu bahwa ia akan hidup kembali pada hari terakhir, ketika orang-orang mati bangkit."

decisions.choice: the resurrection on the last day: the Jewish hope that the dead will be raised at the end of the age
decisions.reason: The Scriptures promised that those who sleep in the dust will awake (Daniel 12:2; compare Isaiah 26:19), and many Jews of Jesus's day held this hope (2 Maccabees 7:9, 14). The Pharisees taught it and the Sadducees denied it (Mark 12:18; Acts 23:8). Jesus himself has spoken of raising the dead on the last day (5:28-29; 6:39-40, 44, 54).

decisions.choice: I know: a firm belief, but one that puts the comfort far off
decisions.reason: Martha does not doubt the resurrection. But she hears Jesus's words as a promise for the distant future, which does little for her grief now. Jesus's answer brings that hope into the present, in himself (verses 25-26).

decisions.choice: when the dead are raised (B); when the dead rise (R)
decisions.reason: "The resurrection" here is the raising of all the dead at the end (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable say what it is. Literal keeps the noun.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "says to him"; Balanced and Readable say "answered" and need no pronoun. The historic present is explained at verse 23.

decisions.choice: cuando resuciten los muertos
decisions.reason: As in English: the raising of all the dead at the end (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "sống lại" for the verb; "sự phục sinh" for the noun anastasis (L, and 11:25)
decisions.reason: "sống lại" is the plain verb; "sự phục sinh" is the noun most readers know for the resurrection, and keeps 11:25 from repeating "sống" three times.

decisions.choice: "... 줄은 (저도) 압니다"
decisions.reason: The particle "은" gives Korean the note of the meaning decision: a firm belief, but one that puts the comfort far off.

decisions.choice: "死んだ人々がよみがえる" (B); "死んだ人たちが生き返る" (R); "復活" (L)
decisions.reason: "The resurrection" is the raising of all the dead at the end (m1); Balanced and Readable say what it is, Literal keeps the noun.

source.text: εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀνάστασις καὶ ἡ ζωή· ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ κἂν ἀποθάνῃ ζήσεται, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ζῶν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ ἀποθάνῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα· πιστεύεις τοῦτο;

records.literal_gloss: Said to her the Jesus, "I am the resurrection and the life; the [one] believing in me even if he dies will live, \v 26 and every [one] living and believing in me not not will die to the age; do you believe this?"

en.L: Jesus said to her, "I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, even if {{gender:they die|he dies}}, will live; \v 26 and everyone who lives and believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will never die. Do you believe this?"
en.B: Jesus said to her, "I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, even if they die, will live, \v 26 and all who live and believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will never die. Do you believe this?"
en.R: Jesus said to her, "I am the resurrection, and I am the life. Whoever believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will live, even if {{gender:they die|he dies}}. \v 26 And everyone who lives and believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will never die. Do you believe this?"

es.L: Le dijo Jesús: «Yo soy la resurrección y la vida; el que cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, aunque muera, vivirá; \v 26 y todo el que vive y cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no morirá jamás. ¿Crees esto?».
es.B: Jesús {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Yo soy la resurrección y la vida. Los que creen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, aunque mueran, vivirán, \v 26 y todos los que viven y creen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} nunca morirán. ¿Crees esto?».
es.R: Jesús {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Yo soy la resurrección, y yo soy la vida. Quien cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} vivirá, aunque muera. \v 26 Y todo el que vive y cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} nunca morirá. ¿Crees esto?».

fr.L: Jésus lui dit : « Je suis la résurrection et la vie. Celui qui croit en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, même s’il meurt, vivra ; \v 26 et quiconque vit et croit en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne mourra absolument jamais. Crois-tu cela ? »
fr.B: Jésus lui dit : « Je suis la résurrection et la vie. Ceux qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, même s’ils meurent, vivront, \v 26 et tous ceux qui vivent et croient en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne mourront jamais. Crois-tu cela ? »
fr.R: Jésus lui a dit : « Je suis la résurrection, et je suis la vie. Ceux qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} vivront, même s’ils meurent. \v 26 Et tous ceux qui vivent et croient en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne mourront jamais. Est-ce que tu crois cela ? »

sw.L: Yesu akamwambia, "Mimi ni ufufuo na uzima. Yule anayeniamini, hata akifa, ataishi; \v 26 na kila aliye hai na kuniamini hatakufa kamwe milele. Je, unaamini hili?"
sw.B: Yesu akamwambia, "Mimi ni ufufuo na uzima. Wanaoniamini, hata wakifa, wataishi, \v 26 na wote walio hai na kuniamini hawatakufa kamwe. Je, unaamini hili?"
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia, "Mimi ni ufufuo, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} ni uzima. Yeyote anayeniamini ataishi, hata akifa. \v 26 Na kila aliye hai na kuniamini hatakufa kamwe. Je, unaamini hili?"

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói với cô: "Ta là sự phục sinh và sự sống. Người nào tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, dù có chết, cũng sẽ sống; \v 26 và mọi người đang sống và tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nhất định không bao giờ chết. Con có tin điều này không?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với cô: "Ta là sự phục sinh và sự sống. Ai tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì dù có chết cũng sẽ sống, \v 26 và ai đang sống mà tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không bao giờ chết. Con có tin điều này không?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với cô: "Ta là sự phục sinh, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là sự sống. Ai tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì sẽ sống, dù người ấy có chết đi. \v 26 Và ai đang sống và tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không bao giờ chết. Con có tin điều này không?"

ko.L: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "나는 부활이고 생명이다. 나를 믿는 사람은 죽는다 해도 살 것이다. \v 26 또 살아 있으면서 나를 믿는 사람은 모두 영원히 결코 죽지 않을 것이다. 너는 이것을 믿느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 마르다에게 말씀하셨다. "나는 부활이며 생명이다. 나를 믿는 사람은 죽더라도 살 것이며, \v 26 살아 있으면서 나를 믿는 사람은 누구나 영원히 죽지 않을 것이다. 너는 이것을 믿느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 마르다에게 말씀하셨다. "나는 부활이다. 그리고 나는 생명이다. 나를 믿는 사람은 죽더라도 다시 살 것이다. \v 26 살아서 나를 믿는 사람은 누구든지 절대로 죽지 않을 것이다. 너는 이것을 믿느냐?"

pt.L: Jesus lhe disse: "Eu sou a ressurreição e a vida. Quem crê em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, ainda que morra, viverá; \v 26 e todo aquele que vive e crê em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} de modo nenhum morrerá, jamais. Você crê nisso?"
pt.B: Jesus lhe disse: "Eu sou a ressurreição e a vida. Os que creem em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, mesmo que morram, viverão, \v 26 e todos os que vivem e creem em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} nunca morrerão. Você crê nisso?"
pt.R: Jesus disse a ela: "Eu sou a ressurreição, e eu sou a vida. Quem crê em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} vai viver, mesmo que morra. \v 26 E todo aquele que vive e crê em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} nunca vai morrer. Você acredita nisso?"

am.L: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ አላት፦ «እኔ ትንሣኤና ሕይወት ነኝ፤ በእኔ የሚያምን ቢሞት እንኳ በሕይወት ይኖራል፤ \v 26 በሕይወት የሚኖርና በእኔ የሚያምን ሁሉ ለዘላለም ከቶ አይሞትም፤ ይህን ታምኛለሽ?»

am.R: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ አላት፦ «እኔ ትንሣኤ ነኝ፤ ሕይወትም እኔ ነኝ። በእኔ የሚያምን ሰው ቢሞት እንኳ በሕይወት ይኖራል። \v 26 በሕይወት ያለና በእኔ የሚያምን ሁሉ ፈጽሞ አይሞትም። ይህን ታምኛለሽ?»

hi.L: यीशु ने उससे कहा, "मैं पुनरुत्थान और जीवन हूँ। जो मुझ पर विश्वास करता है, वह चाहे मर भी जाए, फिर भी जीएगा; \v 26 और हर एक जो जीवित है और मुझ पर विश्वास करता है, कभी नहीं मरेगा। क्या तुम इस पर विश्वास करती हो?"
hi.B: यीशु ने उससे कहा, "मैं पुनरुत्थान और जीवन हूँ। जो मुझ पर विश्वास करते हैं, वे चाहे मर भी जाएँ, फिर भी जीएँगे, \v 26 और जो जीवित हैं और मुझ पर विश्वास करते हैं, वे कभी नहीं मरेंगे। क्या तुम इस बात पर विश्वास करती हो?"
hi.R: यीशु ने उससे कहा, "मैं पुनरुत्थान हूँ, और मैं ही जीवन हूँ। जो कोई मुझ पर विश्वास करता है, वह जीएगा, चाहे वह मर भी जाए। \v 26 और हर कोई जो जीवित है और मुझ पर विश्वास करता है, कभी नहीं मरेगा। क्या तुम इस पर विश्वास करती हो?"

ru.L: Сказал ей Иисус: «Я — воскресение и жизнь. Верующий в {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}, даже если умрёт, будет жить; \v 26 и всякий живущий и верующий в {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} никак не умрёт вовек. Веришь ли ты этому?»
ru.B: Иисус сказал ей: «Я — воскресение и жизнь. Тот, кто верит в {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}, даже если умрёт, будет жить, \v 26 и всякий, кто живёт и верит в {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}, никогда не умрёт. Веришь ли ты в это?»

decisions.choice: the resurrection and the life (SBLGNT)
alternatives: I am the resurrection (a few early witnesses)
decisions.reason: A few early witnesses lack "and the life": Papyrus 45, one Old Latin manuscript, the Sinaitic Syriac and the church writer Cyprian. Nearly all other manuscripts, including the earliest papyrus of John (Papyrus 66) and Papyrus 75, have the words. A footnote gives the shorter reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: I am the resurrection and the life: Jesus himself is the life that overcomes death
decisions.reason: With a predicate, "I am" is ordinary grammar (see 6:35); this is the fifth of John's sayings of this kind. Martha placed resurrection at the last day (verse 24); Jesus answers that it is present in him now. The Father has given the Son to have life in himself and to give life to whom he wills (5:21, 26), and the raising of Lazarus will show it.

decisions.choice: two sides of one promise: the believer who dies will live; the believer who lives will never die
alternatives: both halves speak of the resurrection at the last day
the second half promises that believers living now will not die physically
decisions.reason: The first half speaks of bodily death: those who believe in Jesus will die, as Lazarus has, yet they will live, raised to life (5:28-29; 6:40). The second half speaks of a different death: whoever is alive and believes will never die in the sense that matters, cut off from God's life, because they already have eternal life (5:24; 8:51). Jesus does not deny that believers die; he denies that death can end the life he gives.

decisions.choice: lives and believes: one person, alive now and believing
alternatives: lives with the life Jesus gives
decisions.reason: One article governs both verbs, describing the same person. "Lives" most likely means is alive in this life, set against "even if he dies" in the first half. It may instead mean lives with the life Jesus gives, which comes by believing; the promise is the same either way, and every level keeps the open wording.

decisions.choice: never die: the strongest denial, for all time
alternatives: will not die forever (death will not be permanent)
decisions.reason: Two negatives stand together, the strongest way of denying that something will happen, and "to the age" adds "for all time". The same idiom is used in 8:51-52, 10:28 and 13:8, where it plainly means "never".

decisions.choice: do you believe this?: Jesus asks for Martha's own faith
decisions.reason: The question is personal and in the present tense. Martha has spoken of what she knows (verses 22 and 24); Jesus asks whether she trusts him now, and her answer is a confession of who he is (verse 27).

decisions.choice: even if {{gender:they die|he dies}}
decisions.reason: The one who believes may be a man or a woman, so the pronoun takes the gender setting, with the traditional "he dies" as the alternative. Balanced uses the plural "those who believe", which is already inclusive and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: even if
decisions.reason: The Greek states a condition, "even if", rather than a concession; every level keeps it, rather than the familiar "though".

decisions.choice: I am the resurrection, and I am the life
alternatives: I raise the dead and give life
decisions.reason: Readable keeps both nouns, since Jesus names himself, not only what he does, and repeats "I am" to make the two halves clear (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: aunque muera, no gender setting
decisions.reason: Spanish "aunque muera" needs no pronoun, so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: aunque
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the condition "even if" (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Celui qui croit ... même s’il meurt (L), with no gender setting; Ceux qui croient ... même s’ils meurent (R)
decisions.reason: The believer may be a man or a woman. English needs the gender setting for "he"; in French "il" after "celui qui" is grammatical agreement with a word that already covers everyone, as in 11:9-10, so Literal needs no setting. Readable uses the plural, as Balanced does in both languages.

decisions.choice: ne mourra absolument jamais (L); ne mourront jamais (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 10:28: Literal adds "absolument" to show the double negative with "for ever" (meaning decision m5); Balanced and Readable say "jamais", which already means "never, for all time".

decisions.choice: no gender spans in this chapter
decisions.reason: The English needs "they" with "he" as the traditional alternative here and in verses 9-10 and 57. Swahili verbs (a-kifa, a-tamwambia) say nothing about sex, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "dù có chết" / "dù người ấy có chết" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender setting span as in English
decisions.reason: Vietnamese needs no gendered pronoun here (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: "Con" for Martha in Jesus's question
decisions.reason: Style guide section 6 allows "con" for one person where relation requires; Jesus speaks to Martha as a teacher to a believer who calls herself "con".

decisions.choice: "부활" and "생명" at every level
decisions.reason: "부활" is the established word for anastasis and Martha has just used it (11:24); "생명" is the book-wide word for zoe.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "나를 믿는 사람은 죽더라도"
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean needs no pronoun after "사람" (person), so there are not two ways of saying it (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: "다시 살 것이다" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds 다시 so that new readers see that life after death is meant.

decisions.choice: ainda que morra (L); mesmo que morra (R), with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs a setting for the pronoun after "the one who believes". Portuguese "quem crê ... ainda que morra" has no pronoun and already means any man or woman, so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: Você crê nisso?
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to Martha with "você", as to any one person (style section 4), and so says "o seu irmão" in verse 23, while she answers him with "tu". The difference in address is the Portuguese convention, not a difference in warmth.

decisions.choice: "ትንሣኤ" (resurrection) at every level, with the verb "ተነሣ" (rise, 11:23-24)
decisions.reason: "ትንሣኤ" is the living word for the resurrection and shares its root with "ይነሣል" in 11:23-24, so the link between Jesus's promise, Martha's hope and "I am the resurrection" stays visible at every level.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "በእኔ የሚያምን ቢሞት" (the one who believes in me, if he dies)
alternatives: a span like the English {{gender:they die|he dies}}
decisions.reason: The Amharic relative with the generic masculine verb already includes women and men, so there are not two wordings to choose between. Recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: "वह ... मर भी जाए", with no gender span
alternatives: a span like the English "they die|he dies"
decisions.reason: Hindi "वह" and the verb "मर जाए" serve for a man or a woman alike, so there is nothing for the gender setting to change.

decisions.choice: "मैं पुनरुत्थान और जीवन हूँ"; "चाहे ... भी"
decisions.reason: "I am" with a predicate is the ordinary "मैं ... हूँ". "चाहे ... भी" keeps the Greek "even if" (a condition), and the wording stays apart from the familiar older Hindi version.

decisions.choice: "Я — воскресение и жизнь"
decisions.reason: "I am" with a predicate takes the dash (docs/john-terms.md); Readable repeats "я —" so the two halves stand out (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "верующий ..., даже если умрёт" (L); "кто ..., даже если умрёт" (R), with no gender setting
alternatives: a gender setting on the verb
decisions.reason: The English has a gender setting on "they die / he dies". The Russian verb has no gender in the future tense, and "кто" is inclusive, so there is no setting.

decisions.choice: "хто вірить ..., хоч і помре" with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Ukrainian "хто ..., той" and the verb without a pronoun already cover men and women, so the English gender setting has no Ukrainian span here.

decisions.choice: "たとえ死んでも" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs a gender span for its pronoun; Japanese needs no pronoun here, and 者 and 人 are already inclusive, so there is no span. This holds through the passage.

decisions.choice: "わたしが復活である。そして、わたしが命である。" (R)
alternatives: "わたしは復活であり、命である"
decisions.reason: Readable repeats "I am" for each noun, as the English Readable does, and uses が to put the weight on Jesus himself (m2): resurrection is not only a future event but this person. Jesus' speech stays in the plain style.

decisions.choice: I have believed: a settled faith, emphatically her own
alternatives: I have just now come to believe
decisions.reason: The perfect tense describes believing that began in the past and still holds, as in Peter's confession (6:69). The pronoun "I" is written out and emphatic: whatever others think, this is what she believes.

decisions.choice: the Christ, the Son of God, the one coming into the world: the fullest confession of Jesus so far in John
decisions.reason: Martha gathers the titles others have given him: the Christ (1:41), the Son of God (1:34, 49), and the one coming into the world (6:14). John later says that he wrote so that readers would believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God (20:31); Martha says the same words here. She answers Jesus's question not by repeating his saying but by confessing who he is.

decisions.choice: the one coming into the world: the one God promised to send
decisions.reason: "The one who comes" was a way of speaking of the one God would send (6:14; 12:13, quoting Psalm 118:26; Matthew 11:3). John also speaks of the true light "coming into the world" (1:9). "The world" is the world of people, to whom he comes.

decisions.choice: the Son of God: the royal title for the Messiah, which the Gospel fills out
decisions.reason: Beside "the Christ", "Son of God" is first a title of the king God promised (2 Samuel 7:14; Psalm 2:7), as with Nathanael (1:49). John's readers know that Jesus is God's Son in a fuller sense (1:14, 18; 5:18-26).

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: The Greek has the article with the title, so every level writes "the Christ", with "the Messiah" as the setting's alternative (see the book's terms).

decisions.choice: I do believe
decisions.reason: Readable puts the perfect in the present, adding "do" to carry the emphasis of the written-out "I" (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced keep "I have believed", as in 6:69.

decisions.choice: the one God promised to send into the world
alternatives: the one who is coming into the world
decisions.reason: As at 6:14: Readable explains who "the one coming" is. Martha knew the expectation, so this puts nothing in her mouth that she did not know.

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}
decisions.reason: A title with the article, as at 1:20.

decisions.choice: el que Dios prometió enviar al mundo
decisions.reason: As at 6:14: Readable explains who "the one coming" is (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: moi, je crois (L, B); je crois (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek perfect speaks of a faith that began in the past and still holds (meaning decision m1). French "j’ai cru que tu es" is not idiomatic, and "j’ai cru que tu étais" would mean "I thought (wrongly) that you were", so every level uses the present, which says that the faith holds now. Literal and Balanced keep the emphatic "I" with "moi, je". The title has the article, so "le" stands outside the christos setting.

decisions.choice: "{{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}" for "the Christ"
decisions.reason: Style guide sections 5 and 7: "Đấng" marks the title, as the article does in Greek, so neither alternative reads as a name.

decisions.choice: "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}(이시고)" with no word for "the"
decisions.reason: Korean has no article and reads the title as a title; the honorific copula "-이시-" follows either alternative correctly.

decisions.choice: "믿고 있습니다" (L); "믿습니다" (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek perfect is a settled faith that still holds; Korean "믿었습니다" would sound finished, so the present is used.

decisions.choice: eu tenho crido (L); Eu creio (B); Eu creio, sim (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek perfect is a faith that began and still holds (meaning decision m1). Portuguese "eu cri" would put it wholly in the past; Literal uses the compound "tenho crido", which reaches into the present, and Balanced the plain present "creio". Readable adds "sim" for the emphatic written-out "I", as the English Readable adds "do".

decisions.choice: "मसीह", with no christos span
decisions.reason: "मसीह" is both the familiar title and the word Messiah itself, so the choice the English setting offers is already made; the style guide gives Hindi no christos setting.

decisions.choice: "я поверила" (L, B); "я верю" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek perfect is a settled faith, emphatically her own (meaning decision m1). The perfective "поверила" keeps the key verb "верить"; Readable puts it in the present, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "я повірила" (L), "я вірю" (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek perfect is a settled faith, begun and still held (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps the past of the act, Balanced and Readable say the faith that lasts.

decisions.choice: "わたしは……信じてきました" (L); "わたしは信じております" (B); "心から信じています" (R)
decisions.reason: The perfect describes a faith that began and still holds, and "I" is emphatic (m1). Literal shows the lasting past with 〜てきました, Balanced with 〜ております, Readable carries the emphasis with 心から.
